title: De insigni paradoxo, quod in analysi maximorum et minimorum occurrit

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§1–11): Euler studies the functional ∫√x ds, the Maupertuis/Euler action for a heavy body whose speed is √x, with x measured downward from the level of zero velocity. The extremals satisfy √x·dy/ds = √a. They are the parabolas y = 2√(a(x−a)), whose vertex lies at depth a. Along such a parabola, ds = √x dx/√(x−a). So the 'momentum' (value of the functional) from the vertex E to the point of abscissa x is ∫x dx/√(x−a) = (2/3)(2a+x)√(x−a) = (2/(3√a))(2a+x)√(ax−aa).

The end-points are F (abscissa f) and H (abscissa h), with horizontal separation measured by g, so that √(ah−aa) − √(af−aa) = g. On p.21 Euler eliminated the radicals and solved the quadratic in a, getting a = gg/(f+h±2√(fh−gg)). Hence real extremals exist only when fh > gg, and then there are two of them.

This page:
- Write R = √(fh−gg) and D = f+h+2R. Euler uses 2g√(af−aa) = a(h−f) − gg. Since fD − gg = (f+R)², the root comes out negative: √(af−aa) = −g(f+R)/D. Then √(ah−aa) = g + √(af−aa) = g(h+R)/D. So F lies on the far branch of the parabola, on the other side of the vertex from H.
- §12: the momentum of arc FH is the difference of the vertex-based momenta: (2/(3√a))[2a(√(ah−aa) − √(af−aa)) + h√(ah−aa) − f√(af−aa)].
- Substituting the radicals gives (2g/(3D√a))[2aD + ff + hh + (f+h)R].
- Continued on p.23: aD = gg. Rationalising by (f+h−2R), the numerator becomes (4gg+(h−f)²)(f+h−R) and the denominator (h−f)²+4gg. So the momentum is (2g/(3√a))(f+h−R) = (2/3)(f+h−R)√(f+h+2R).
- The other root gives (2/3)(f+h+R)√(f+h−2R).

Purpose: to exhibit that two different curves both satisfy the 'minimum' condition and to compare their values. Euler's §13 links this to the two projectile trajectories with the same launch speed hitting a given target, and their nonexistence beyond a certain range.

Check: with S = f+h, the difference of squares M₊² − M₋² equals 4R³ > 0. So the root a = gg/(S+2R) (smaller a, higher apex: the lofted trajectory) gives the larger action. That lofted arc is the one containing a conjugate point (tangency with the envelope 'parabola of safety') before H, consistent with Jacobi's later theory. This comparison is not on this page.
errors: Printed misprint: 'ob x = gg/(f+h+2√(hf−gg))' should read 'ob a = …'.
Printed misprint in the first displayed value: '√(af−aa) = −(fg − g√(fh−gg))/(…)' should be −(fg + g√(fh−gg))/(…). Euler's own restatement a line later, −g(f+√…)/(…), is correct.
Printed misprint in the formula for FH: 'f√(af−hh)' should be 'f√(af−aa)'.
Typographical 'b' for 'h' in denominators. This is a font/print confusion; no mathematical effect.
All algebra checks out once these misprints are corrected: (f+R)² = fD − gg, √(ah−aa) = g(h+R)/D, and the final momentum (2/3)(f+h−R)√(f+h+2R).

ideas.what: Evaluation of the action ∫√x ds along a parabolic extremal in closed form, (2/3)(2a+x)√(x−a)
ideas.modern_name: Value of the Maupertuis/Jacobi action along a projectile trajectory (two-point action function)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 Methodus inveniendi, Additamentum II on the principle of least action); two-point action functions later Hamilton/Jacobi
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (E65), Additamentum II; E735 itself (Opera postuma 1862 / Mémoires 1811)

ideas.what: Explicit value of the action for both extremal parabolas through two given points, (2/3)(f+h∓R)√(f+h±2R), R = √(fh−gg)
ideas.modern_name: Multi-valued two-point characteristic (action) function; two branches of the extremal field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hamilton (characteristic function, 1834); Jacobi (1837) for analysis of second variation

ideas.what: Recognition that two distinct extremals join F to H, so 'satisfying the Euler equation' cannot guarantee a minimum
ideas.modern_name: Non-sufficiency of the Euler–Lagrange equation; conjugate points / envelope (Jacobi condition)
ideas.where_published: E735 (the paradox is the theme of the paper; discussed in histories of the calculus of variations, details unsure)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful, correct algebra (modulo printer's misprints) evaluating the action on the two extremal parabolas. The conceptual point — two extremals, a pre-Jacobi glimpse of conjugate points — is the known theme of E735 and is acknowledged in histories of the calculus of variations. Nothing on this specific page appears to be an uncredited result.
